identity.real_world_identity_notes: Updated version of the AMG GT3 introduced for 2020, retaining the naturally aspirated V8 and the sequential six-speed rear transaxle of the car it revises. The registered manufacturer page documents the GT3 family transmission rather than the Evo update specifically.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: The 2020 operation manual requires the driver to press and ease the clutch when engaging first gear from rest. It does not establish anti-stall or an automated launch procedure.
No throttle lift is required on upshifts and no manual blip on downshifts, because the drive detected automatic cut and automatic blip. This matches every other curated paddle-shift GT3 car.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.mercedes-amg-gt3-evo.20260813t160217236z-ff03d88a by Jason Kinslow.

overrides.condition: AMS2 1.6.9.91 accepted clutch-free move-off with automatic clutch and shifting disabled.

confidence.basis: Simulator behavior was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world six-speed sequential paddle transmission is established by a registered source.

notes: Observed live in ACC 21257365 via guided verification observation acc.mercedes-amg-gt3-evo-2020.20260823t011325563z-afff3f23 by Jason Kinslow.

overrides.condition: ACC accepted the guided full-throttle clutchless upshift while the authentic lift claim remains open.

confidence.basis: Mercedes-AMG establishes the GT3 family transmission. ACC's visible 2020 selection and its telemetry name, Evo internal id and GT3 class identify the update already curated from AMS2; the guided drive directly established ACC behavior.

claims.basis: The registered source establishes the real-world identity and transmission, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.

The manufacturer specifies a sequential six-speed racing gearbox in a rear transaxle for the AMG GT3 family, of which the Evo is the updated version; the live drive confirmed six paddle gears and clutch-free move-off.
Directly observed during the guided drive: running-shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.
The exact 2020 operation manual instructs the driver to press the clutch before engaging first gear and ease it in to move away; it does not establish anti-stall or an automated launch.

ACC visibly labels the selection `AMG GT3 (2020)` while SimHub reported telemetry name `Mercedes AMG GT3 Evo 2020`, internal id `mercedes_amg_gt3_evo`, and class `GT3`. The combined UI year and telemetry Evo token distinguish it from the original AMG GT3.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

deviations.basis: Whether the car needs a throttle lift on upshifts is not established. A guided drive settles it, by holding the throttle through an upshift and seeing whether the gear engages.

notes: The wheel-rim shape was originally recorded as "gt-style". The separate "gt-style", "formula" and "prototype" values described the same rim: molded grips at 9 and 3 with a control face between them, usually carrying a display and rev lights. They are merged into "gt-formula". The rim was not observed again and nothing about the observation changed.
driver_summary: Paddle sequential with one job left for your left foot, which is the clutch to pull away. After that it cuts the upshift and blips the downshift on its own.
